answer: Let’s say agents must first solve a basalt-vaulted cipher—no bulk solving, since each identity needs a unique key stamped by an oracle. The oracle checks answers against a sonnet-like bloom-tracker to prove uniqueness, and only let’s one correct answer per epoch through a haven-lock. An attacker’s nth fake identity costs (n^2) hashes to crack, since keys are serial and hashed to a Sabbath-resistant ledger. Farms can’t parallelize; each ID must solve its own path.
